title: Found their hoodie in the laundry
old_caption: Found their hoodie and suddenly you're writing a novel? A hoodie text is fine. The "also, I miss you" part belongs with a friend.

title: Big news, wrong first call
old_caption: Good news and your first instinct is to tell them. Share the win where it gets cheered: the people who were there all year.

title: They liked your story
old_caption: One like, forty theories. A like says "I saw it" and that's all. Go to dinner. Save this for the next time your phone lights up.

title: The photo memory hit
old_caption: When the old photo pops up and it hurts. Missing a good day doesn't mean going back. Keep the memory, and tell a friend instead.

title: It's cold and you miss them
old_caption: Cold nights make everything feel like missing someone. Sometimes you miss being warm. Make the soup and share it with someone near.

title: The closure essay, draft twelve
old_caption: Twelve drafts in and the closure essay has footnotes. If you've already said it, a reply won't bring the peace. Read it out loud, then let it go.

title: They're dating someone new
old_caption: They moved on and it stings. Hurt and angry can both be true. Move it out of your body, then call someone who loves you.

title: Their birthday reminder
old_caption: The calendar remembers their birthday even when you're trying not to. You can wish someone well without sending a thing.

title: At the café you planned to visit
old_caption: You made it to the café from the old list, on your own. An old plan can become a new memory that's just yours.

title: Midnight countdown, thumb on send
old_caption: Midnight, confetti, and the urge to text them "new start?" Start the year with the people standing next to you.
